plain_definition_en: Water held underground in soil and rock, pumped up through wells.
A layer of rock or sediment that holds and passes groundwater. Qatar's main ones are Rus and Umm er Radhuma.
Water that refills an aquifer, mainly from rain soaking into the ground.
How much can be pumped each year without depleting the aquifer. In Qatar, recharge minus natural outflow: 74.7 - 25.1 = 49.6 million m3 a year.
Water pumped out of an aquifer. In Qatar the figures are estimates, because wells aren't metered yet.
How much salt is dissolved in water. High salinity harms crops and soil.
The total amount of dissolved minerals and salts, in mg/L. It describes taste and salinity, not whether water is safe to drink.
How well water conducts electricity, which rises with dissolved salt. Sensors measure EC and estimate TDS from it.
Compares sodium with calcium and magnesium. High SAR makes soil seal up so water soaks in poorly.
How acidic or alkaline water is, from 0 to 14, where 7 is neutral.
How cloudy water is, measured in NTU.
Water saltier than fresh water but less salty than seawater. Most of Qatar's groundwater is brackish.
Removing salt from seawater or brackish water. It supplies Qatar's drinking water.
Wastewater cleaned at treatment plants, reused for irrigation, landscaping and aquifer recharge.
Seawater moving into a coastal aquifer when pumping lowers the fresh water level.
Deliberately putting water into an aquifer through recharge wells or basins, to store it or improve it.
The top of the groundwater, below which the ground is fully saturated.
A concentration below which a substance is not expected to harm health. WHO sets none for TDS.
Applying extra water so salts are washed below the root zone.
How much salinity a crop can take before its yield drops. Date palms tolerate far more than most vegetables.
Mainly calcium and magnesium in water. It causes scale and affects taste.
A nitrogen compound from fertiliser or sewage. WHO's drinking-water guideline is 50 mg/L.
Freshwater taken out as a share of the freshwater available (SDG 6.4.2).
Adjusting a sensor against known standard solutions so its readings are accurate.
A slow change in a sensor's readings that does not come from the water, such as fouling or ageing.
